recent_works.title: Correction: Passive Attitude Control of Dust Particles for Active Debris Removal
Passive Attitude Control of Dust Particles for Active Debris Removal
recent_works.abstract: The deployment of micron-sized dust particles for the active removal of small-scale orbital debris (ranging from 1 mm to 1 cm) calls for the development of accurate attitude dynamics models. Such models must account for the dominant environmental torques acting on design-specific micro particles. This study presents the development of a simulation framework aimed at investigating passive attitude stabilization mechanisms for dust particles. The primary objective is to analyze the influence of environmental torques on rotational dynamics in relation to engineered particle properties.

recent_works.title: Coupled Orbit-Attitude Periodic Motion in the Earth-Moon System With Solar Radiation Pressure Torque
recent_works.abstract: Growing interest in lunar missions drives the need for low-propellant missions to extend spacecraft life and mission duration. Propellant resupply in cislunar space is challenging, and carrying excess fuel penalizes payload mass. Nevertheless, station-keeping is necessary to maintain orbits in this chaotic dynamical region, and attitude management is another significant driver of propellant consumption. Decreasing the demand on the attitude control system will not only reduce propellant consumption but also increase the lifetime of failure-prone devices, such as reaction wheels. Conserved propellant can then be allocated for station-keeping and increasing mission life. Naturally periodic motion can reduce the demand for station-keeping and attitude corrections. This paper expands existing research on Earth-Moon coupled orbit-attitude periodic motion by including the next largest perturbation on attitude motion: solar radiation pressure (SRP) torque. Methodologies to search for, correct, and build families of periodic solutions are proposed.

recent_works.title: Dynamic Ecosystems for Mars ECLSS Testing, Evaluation, and Reliability (DEMETER): A Proposed Human-Mars Precursor Bioregenerative ECLSS Technology Demonstration Mission
recent_works.abstract: Dynamic Ecosystems for Mars ECLSS Testing, Evaluation, and Reliability (DEMETER) is a proposed uncrewed advanced science mission and technology demonstration targeting launch in the early 2040s, to showcase the operation of a novel bioregenerative, aquatic plant-based, life support system capable of simultaneously converting carbon dioxide into oxygen, remediating wastewater, and closing nutrient cycles by producing food from human metabolic waste on the Martian surface. This proposed two-year mission would demonstrate the successful transfer of plants to Mars, the propagation of plants in an enclosed capsule on the Martian surface, the assimilation of Martian carbon dioxide into edible biomass while concurrently producing oxygen, and the phytoremediation of simulated gray and black wastewater in preparation for the full use of this biological life support system (BLSS) in conjunction with crewed missions to Mars.

recent_works.title: On the spin-orbit problem for highly elliptical orbits and recursive excitation
recent_works.abstract: Examining the spin-orbit coupling effects for highly elliptical orbits is relevant to the mission design and operation of cislunar space assets, such as the Lunar Gateway. In high-eccentricity orbits, the gravity-gradient moment is here modelled as an instantaneous excitation at each periapsis passage. By approximating the gravity-gradient moment through Dirac pulses, we derive a recursive discrete map describing the rotational state of the satellite at the periapsis passage. Thanks to the recursive map, we are able to find the initial attitude corresponding to an unbounded growth of angular velocity, and to identify initial conditions whose evolution is such that the pulses have the same sign (in-phase condition) or the alternate sign (counterphase condition) at successive periapsis passages. In the recursive map, we perform the numerical analysis up to ten periapsis passages. In order to justify the introduction of the discrete map, we compare the results of the discrete map with those found in the spin-orbit problem.
